name: Crack a fetch on turn 1-2 for a shockland that unlocks a hand card, when no basic reaches it
intent: Review item 3's fallback: once open-fetch-unlocks was narrowed to unlocks_by_basic_search (never cracking a fetch for nothing when the library holds no reachable basic), a hand fetch whose own search can reach an unlock only through a non-basic land - a shockland the library holds, no basic - needed a play of its own, or that unlock would go begging entirely. Plays a fetch from hand and cracks it for whatever library land unlocks some other hand card, paying life for both the fetch's own find (when it is itself a shock) and, if the found land also enters only untapped_if_paid, that land's own life cost too - strictly the most expensive of the fetch family, so it stands down whenever anything cheaper covers the same unlock: open-land-unlocks (a free untapped land), open-shock-unlocks (a hand shockland already reaches the unlock directly, one payment instead of two), and open-fetch-unlocks (the fetch can reach a basic instead, free). instant-reanimator carries exactly one copy each of Island, Plains and Swamp, so no fetch is more precious than another the way a scarcer basic makes one elsewhere in this pass - the prefer list is left empty and ties: any breaks it by sorted name, the same reasoning open-fetch-unlocks itself uses. The crack itself is restricted to an untapped source that can actually reach the unlock (searches_for_any plus unlocks_by_search, the broader key, since this play exists precisely for the fetch that cannot reach a basic). Its own choose_cards pick uses the same three-tier order as open-fetch-unlocks (a Plains-subtype shock first, then a bare basic as a defensive no-op the true condition already guarantees will never match, then any shockland), paying life. Stands down at 7 life or less and once the library is down to 5 cards or fewer. Only turns 1-2, land drop available, mine, precombat main, empty stack. Stands down once the discard outlet (a creature with an own +1/+1-counter-put ability, Psychic Frog in this 60) is already on the battlefield: that fact is byte-identical to the seat-admitted bin-fatty-vs-permanent-exile play's own battlefield-outlet true key, and it can never hold on a genuine turn 1-2 board anyway - the outlet costs two mana and has to survive a turn cycle before that play reads it as safe to fire, so this key costs this play nothing here and only prevents the two plays overlapping later in the game.
